## The question

How did sales change over the first six months of the year?
This example uses fictional data stored directly in the document.

## Prepare the data

```{python}
#| label: prepare-data
months = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]
sales = [120, 135, 128, 160, 175, 190]
growth = (sales[-1] / sales[0] - 1) * 100
print(f"Total sales: {sum(sales):,} units")
print(f"Change from January to June: {growth:.1f}%")
```

## Monthly values

The following cell generates a Markdown table from the data.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-sales
#| tbl-cap: "Fictional monthly sales"
#| output: asis
print("| Month | Units sold |")
print("|:------|-----------:|")
for month, units in zip(months, sales):
    print(f"| {month} | {units} |")
```

## Visualize the trend

```{python}
#| label: fig-sales
#| fig-cap: "Sales rise overall, with a small dip in March."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
ax.plot(months, sales, marker="o", color="#2563eb", linewidth=2)
ax.set(xlabel="Month", ylabel="Units sold", title="Monthly sales")
ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Interpretation

@fig-sales shows an upward trend overall. @tbl-sales provides the underlying
values. Change the `sales` list and render again to update the calculations,
table, and chart together.
